Nearly two dozen states are suing to block a new rule that would push some 80,000 people
out of federally subsidized housing, including many children who are U.S. citizens.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports the Trump administration wants to ban families with any member who
does not have legal immigration status.
Immigrants in the U.S. unlawfully do not get federal rental aid, but in 1997, Congress
said they can live with family members who do.
The Trump administration calls this a loophole and argues it's not fair to American taxpayers,
especially given the high demand and long waitlist for a housing subsidy.
But 22 mostly Democratic-led states say pushing out such families goes against what Congress
intended and they say it would leave many HUD residents homeless.
The new rule also requires HUD tenants to verify their citizenship status with the federal
database, but the state's lawsuit says that database has a documented record of errors.
Jennifer Ludden in Pierre News, Washington.
Honda is recalling more than 810,000 vehicles for possibly defective airbag inflators.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration says the vehicles have certain Takata front
and passenger airbag inflators that could rupture and cause metal fragments to cause serious
injuries to occupants.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
Native ants play critical roles in maintaining the fabric of many ecosystems, but that fabric
can unravel when invasive ants show up.
Here's our science reporter Ari Daniel.
College's Deafu Chen of the South China Agricultural University and his colleagues examined the
long-term interactions between native ant communities in Southeast China and two nasty
invasive species, including the little fire ants.
When these ants were outnumbered, they played dead and the other invasive species stopped
assailing them.
But once there were four times as many, they launched lethal attacks.
The little fire ants then turned to the native ants, which they displaced or wiped out.
Chen says the results suggest it may be best to counteract the invasive species early before
the native ants come under fire.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
